answer: An agent economy can stagger admission: each epoch grants only a small quota of full voting rights to newcomers, while fresh identities must complete randomized paid micro-tasks before their stake vests. A sybil farmer flooding the network with clones sees that ocean of agents trickle in like water crossing a dune - each batch thin, observable, and priced. Power stays with violet-flagged veterans whose history spans many epochs, so manufactured majorities never outnumber earned trust.
